The premise that the title only moved to the Petronas Towers in 1998 is incorrect. The Petronas Towers are the tallest in the world, but the title of "tallest outside North America" was held by the Bank of China Tower in Hong Kong (completed 1989, height ~367m) from 1989 until 1991, and then by the World Financial Center in New York (which is in North America, so this doesn't count). Actually, the Bank of China Tower in Hong Kong surpassed One Raffles Place (280m) in 1989. The next building outside North America to surpass the Bank of China Tower was the International Commerce Centre in Hong Kong (2010) or perhaps the Shanghai World Financial Center (2008), but the immediate successor to One Raffles Place as the *tallest outside North America* was the Bank of China Tower in Hong Kong. The Planner incorrectly assumes the title went to Kuala Lumpur, ignoring the existence of Hong Kong's skyscrapers which were taller than Singapore's during that period. This error leads the WebSurfer to search for the wrong building (Petronas) and city (Kuala Lumpur), derailing the solution.
